evals.prompt: run vaultwarden on my box
evals.expected_output: The app installed from the Coolify template, with its URL and generated credentials relayed to the user.
expectations: Calls device_status first to see what already runs
Calls workspace_resources before installing and respects its admission result
Uses app_install with the template slug rather than writing compose by hand
Relays the returned URL and one-time credentials to the user immediately
Does not declare failure on a slow first start without checking app_list or app_logs

evals.prompt: self-host this compose file on the device
evals.expected_output: The compose submitted through app_install, with sanitizer rejections explained if any.
expectations: Passes the compose to app_install rather than trying to reach the container engine
On a sanitizer rejection, explains which key was refused and adapts the compose instead of retrying verbatim
Knows published ports are reallocated by the device and reports the actual URL

evals.prompt: watch this apartment listings page every 30 minutes and show new ones on the tv
evals.expected_output: A scheduled task created with an interval schedule and a prompt that casts a summary to the screen.
expectations: Checks a configured agent with a headless command exists, or configures one with the user
Uses schedule=interval with interval_minutes, not a bespoke loop
Writes a task prompt that includes casting the result to a screen
Recognizes creation queues the first run; checks task_runs without starting a duplicate run or claiming completion

evals.prompt: the task needs my listings-site password
evals.expected_output: The secret stored by name and referenced from the task, never echoed back.
expectations: Uses secret_set and references the name in the task's secrets
Never prints or reads back the secret value
Explains the value is write-only on the device

evals.prompt: remove the uptime kuma app and its data
evals.expected_output: Removal only after the user confirms the data loss.
expectations: Confirms purge with the user before calling app_remove with purge=true
Explains data is kept when purge is false

evals.prompt: what is my box running right now
evals.expected_output: A summary of apps, scheduled tasks and coding sessions from the inventory.
expectations: Calls device_status and reads apps, tasks and coding_sessions from it
Reports paused tasks (enabled=false) and last run outcomes, not just names

evals.prompt: Stop the current rentals task run but keep its schedule. Show me its log.
evals.expected_output: Current run stopped, schedule retained, and its log read.
expectations: Uses task_stop, not task_delete or enabled=false
Uses task_runs to obtain a run ID, then task_run_log

evals.prompt: Set LOG_LEVEL=debug for just my dashboard app as a non-secret variable.
evals.expected_output: Targeted readable var stored for the app.
expectations: Uses secret_set with domain=app, target=dashboard and secret=false
Explains that affected app configuration is reloaded

evals.prompt: Continue my device Tasks assistant conversation with: check why rentals failed.
evals.expected_output: Message sent to the existing fixed Tasks chat.
expectations: Uses chat_list or chat_history to inspect the tasks chat
Calls chat_send with id=tasks
Treats accepted message as pending and reads chat_history for the eventual reply

evals.prompt: Deploy this repository on my box and inspect the Dockerfile first.
evals.expected_output: App source fetched and inspected before deploying compose with a source build.
expectations: Uses app_source_fetch and app_source_read
Allows build context ./src
Checks app_list phase and last_error before claiming readiness

evals.prompt: Disable automatic repair for my rentals task but leave it running on schedule.
evals.expected_output: Automatic task repair disabled without pausing the schedule.
expectations: Uses task_update with self_heal=false
Does not set enabled=false or delete the task

evals.prompt: Show which secrets my rentals task uses and whether it catches up after reboot.
evals.expected_output: The requested management workflow completed through the available device tools.
expectations: Reads task_list secrets and catch_up_on_boot; does not infer omitted values
Does not fetch secret values

evals.prompt: Set up an ntfy alerts channel for my task and send a test.
evals.expected_output: The requested management workflow completed through the available device tools.
expectations: Uses notify_channel_add then notify_channel_test
Reads notify_channels for delivery health
Does not echo credential-bearing URLs

evals.prompt: Change my existing nightly backup to every hour and keep everything else.
evals.expected_output: The requested management workflow completed through the available device tools.
expectations: Finds the job ID with app_backups
Calls app_backup_update with schedule kind=interval and interval_minutes=60
Does not resubmit or overwrite destination credentials

evals.prompt: Restore yesterday’s notes backup into a separate app named notes-recovered.
evals.expected_output: The requested management workflow completed through the available device tools.
expectations: Lists versions and apps before selecting the restore point
Uses app_backup_restore with as_new=notes-recovered
Treats acceptance as background work and reads app_backups for the result

evals.prompt: Which models can my configured agent use, and which branches exist in acme/app?
evals.expected_output: The requested management workflow completed through the available device tools.
expectations: Uses agent_models for the configured agent
Uses git_repos and git_branches with the connected host
Does not request a new API key for an already configured agent

evals.prompt: Install this Drone runner compose; its runner declares a container engine so it can launch build jobs.
evals.expected_output: The compose is installed with the workspace's managed app-private container capability.
expectations: Submits the compose through app_install and lets the workspace provide its managed isolated capability
Does not add privileged mode, a nested daemon, or host-engine access
Explains that the capability follows the app lifecycle without exposing internal implementation details

evals.prompt: My nightly task needs to log into the installed inventory app and keep the returned API token without showing it.
evals.expected_output: The task calls the internal app API and saves the token directly into encrypted task credentials.
expectations: Uses task_secret_list to discover existing task credential names
Uses app_request with secret references for login inputs
Uses app_request save_response for the returned token instead of printing it or copying it through chat

evals.prompt: Send my general Tarvis chat: build an expense tracker in a new project.
evals.expected_output: The request is sent to the general chat, which can hand implementation to one separate Code session.
expectations: Uses chat_send rather than directly invoking the chat-internal continue_in_code tool
Recognizes the handoff keeps the original general chat and creates a separate coding session using the same agent/model
Does not create a duplicate second session when the handoff is repeated

evals.prompt: The watcher found two pending listings, sent one alert, then notification delivery failed on the other.
evals.expected_output: Only successfully processed and delivered items are acknowledged; failed delivery remains pending.
expectations: Treats task_memory_new results as pending until acknowledged
Calls task_memory_ack only for the item whose required delivery succeeded
Leaves the failed item unacknowledged for retry
